newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsicans get free electricity in labour dispute.
newsitem.headline: Corsicans get free electricity in labour dispute.

text.p: Corsicans may be getting free electricity due a bitter labour dispute over jobs that has workers at electric utility EDF threatening to take over a power plant on the Mediterranean resort island.

After lengthy talks over a demand for 20 new jobs at EDF, representatives of the Communist-led CGT union announced on Wednesday they would provide free electric service to as much of the island as they could until their demands were met.
EDF officials had agreed to create the 20 new jobs after 16 hours of negotiations and a scuffle in which workers threw bottles and fruit at police, who retaliated with tear gas.
But talks broke down over union demands for a judicial amnesty and payment for strike days. EDF chief negotiator Claude Renault left the site to seek further instructions from Paris headquarters.

Union officials said they would provide service at no cost until the utility agreed to send a new representative to resume talks. Mediator Bernard Fievre said he would do all he could to get the negotiations going again.
